flags.title: Denver / Boulder Housing Cost Crisis — $14.81 Minimum Wage Still Inadequate
flags.summary: Despite a state minimum wage of $14.81/hr and a Denver minimum wage of $18.81/hr, the median rent in Denver exceeds $1,800/month, making housing stability a primary concern. For clients in the Denver/Boulder area, housing stability should be assessed first.

flags.title: Colorado SNAP ABAWD — Active with Limited Waivers
flags.summary: Work requirements for Able-Bodied Adults Without Dependents (ABAWDs) in the Colorado SNAP program are active in most of the state, with limited waivers for some rural counties. The Denver metro area has no waiver.

flags.title: Colorado TANF (Colorado Works) — $508/mo, 60-Month Federal Limit
flags.summary: Colorado's TANF program, known as Colorado Works, provides up to $508/month for a family of three and has a 60-month lifetime limit. The program emphasizes self-sufficiency and support services.

flags.title: Colorado 3-Year Wage SOL (CWCA) — Strategic Advantage
flags.summary: The Colorado Wage Claim Act (CWCA) provides a 3-year statute of limitations for wage claims, which is longer than the federal 2-year limit. This allows workers more time to file claims for back wages.

flags.title: Colorado CCRD — 6-Month SOL for State Civil Rights
flags.summary: The Colorado Civil Rights Division (CCRD) has a very short 6-month statute of limitations for employment and housing discrimination complaints. It is critical to file with the EEOC simultaneously to preserve the 300-day federal deadline.

flags.title: Colorado Unhoused Population — Denver Hub
flags.summary: Colorado has a large unhoused population, concentrated in Denver. The city's shelter system is often at capacity, and the cold weather creates life-safety risks. Immediate routing to shelter and housing services is critical for unhoused clients.

flags.title: Western Slope / Rural Colorado — Geographic Isolation
flags.summary: Rural and mountain communities in Colorado face geographic isolation, with limited access to services and resources. Legal aid and other support services are sparse, and clients may need to travel long distances.

flags.title: Denver Latino/Immigrant Community — Large Population, Specific Routing
flags.summary: The Denver metro area has a large Latino and immigrant population. State law limits data sharing with ICE, and Health First Colorado is available to eligible immigrants. Undocumented adults can receive care at Denver Health FQHCs.

flags.title: Involuntary Hold: Colorado 72-Hour Hold
flags.message: CO involuntary psychiatric hold law: Colorado 72-Hour Hold. Statutory authority: C.R.S. § 27-65-105. Maximum initial hold duration: 72 hours. Legal standard: imminent danger to self/others. A hearing must be held before the hold can be extended. The person has the right to counsel at the hearing.
action_items: Verify hold did not exceed 72 hours without court order
Confirm hearing was held within statutory timeframe
Check that patient rights notice was provided at admission
Request complete hold documentation from facility

flags.title: Psychiatric Patient Rights
flags.message: Psychiatric patients in CO retain fundamental rights during hospitalization: right to communicate with persons outside the facility, right to receive and send mail, right to access legal counsel, right to refuse treatment (with limited exceptions), right to informed consent, right to access medical records, and right to file grievances. These rights cannot be restricted as a condition of treatment.
action_items: Verify patient rights notice was provided and signed
Check whether any rights were restricted and if proper procedures were followed
Confirm access to legal counsel was not impeded

flags.title: Federal Restraint & Seclusion Limits
flags.message: Federal law (42 CFR § 482.13) sets strict limits on restraint and seclusion in CO: physician order required within 1 hour, face-to-face evaluation within 1 hour, continuous monitoring required, maximum 4 hours per order for adults (2 hours for ages 9-17, 1 hour for under 9), and restraint may only be used to protect the patient from harm — never as punishment, convenience, or retaliation.
action_items: Request restraint/seclusion logs for all episodes
Verify physician order was obtained within 1 hour
Check that face-to-face evaluation occurred within 1 hour
Verify restraint was not used as punishment or convenience
Check for injuries during restraint episodes
legal_references: CMS State Operations Manual Appendix A

flags.title: Involuntary Psychiatric Hold Statute
flags.message: This state has specific statutes governing involuntary psychiatric holds. Know the time limits, hearing rights, and appeal procedures before they expire.

flags.title: Mental Health Patient Bill of Rights
flags.message: This state has a Patient Bill of Rights for mental health facilities. Facilities must inform patients of these rights upon admission.
flags.statute: Colorado Mental Health Patient Rights Act

flags.title: Discharge Planning Requirements
flags.message: This state requires facilities to create discharge plans with follow-up appointments, medication management, and community resource referrals.
flags.statute: Colorado Mental Health Discharge Planning Standards
